Three products · one design system

Three products. One way to work.

This is the build reference for OpenBuild, OpenWrite, and OpenDictate. Each tab gives one product. A tab holds a brief, a map, every screen at full size, and the flows a person walks. It also names the states a screen must handle and the checks a team runs before it ships. Every screen uses the design system’s own components, so this document shows what the code can produce. Each flow step names the screen and the state the person sees. The numbers give the order. The chips give the state words the interface shows.

OpenBuild · the console

Brief an agent. Approve what leaves the sandbox. Publish through five gates. Run the apps.

OpenBuild is the workbench and the governance plane. A person briefs an agent in a session. The agent works inside an operating system sandbox. Every action that leaves the sandbox waits for a person. A release passes five evidence-bearing gates. Each published app carries its own key, spend cap, and signed audit chain.

Rule · the sidebar is ink-deep and never scrolls the main pane. Rule · a state word travels with its object. The same chip appears on the sidebar item, the view header, and the audit line. Rule · one signal button in a view: Start session, Publish, or New app from session. An approval card carries its own signal button, Approve once, on every screen. While an approval card shows, the view’s own signal button steps down to .btn--ink. Rule · the right pane is the inspector everywhere. Its tabs are Files · Changes · Terminal · Tool access. Rule · an object has one name everywhere. The full app name appears in the sidebar, the apps card, the table, and the audit line. Rule · the sidebar-foot meter is the only workspace meter. A card never repeats it.

Screens

Four screens and three variants, in the order a person meets them.

Home, the first-run Home, then a session with its focus mode and the palette, then publish, then the apps. This document draws each screen at full size with numbered regions. The table under each screen says what a region shows, how it behaves, and which components build it.

Flows

Five flows carry the product.

Each step names the screen and the state the person sees. The numbers are the order; the chips are the state words the interface shows.

Brief to app

The main path. A small tool takes ten minutes.

  1. Brief. Home. Type the brief. Open the run summary to change the sandbox, the mode, or the model. ⌘↩.idle
  2. Run. Session. The agent works in the sandbox. Tool rows stream in.streaming
  3. Approve. An action leaves the sandbox. The card waits for you.needs you
  4. Review. Inspector · Changes goes wide. Read the diff. Reply to steer.done
  5. Publish. The header offers Publish (⇧⌘P). Five gates. The diffs you read in step 04 count. Record your review at gate 5 of 5.streaming
  6. Run the app. Apps. The app has a key, a cap, and an address.live

Approval

This moment is the reason for the product.

  1. Request. The agent asks to leave the sandbox. The run pauses.needs you
  2. Notice. The sidebar item, the view header, and Home show it. An aria-live="assertive" region announces "Approval needed: network pypi.org. Press ⇧⌘A to go to it."
  3. Decide. Approve once, allow for the session, or deny. Each choice is a button with its key.
  4. Record. The audit line appears with your name. The card turns decided. Allow for session shows a toast with Undo for 8 s.decided
  5. Resume. The run continues. A denied request stays in the agent’s context.streaming

Find

Two keystrokes reach any item.

  1. Open. ⌘K from any screen. The palette lists recent items.
  2. Narrow. Type a name, an #id, or a term: needs:you, app:, state:, gate:. ">" lists commands.
  3. Go. ↩ opens the item. ⌘↩ opens it in focus mode. No match shows the empty state with the terms.

First run

Three steps. No key needed for a local model.

  1. Connect. The console finds the engine on the loopback port. A mock engine shows the warn banner and the mock chip.mock
  2. Choose a model. The banner link opens the local model list with size and a download meter. Providers are optional.downloading
  3. Brief. Home. Start session enables. The banner clears when the first session starts.ready

Cap reached

The apps stay governed when money runs out.

  1. Warn. The meter turns amber at 80%. A warn banner names the app at 88%.live
  2. Stop. At 100% the app pauses and rejects every call. The error banner says why.paused
  3. Decide. "Raise cap →" in the banner opens the in-place confirm; ↩ confirms. Or keep it paused. Both are one audit line. The toast offers Undo for 8 s.live

Build notes

From the current console to this.

Where it lives

Tokens. shared/styles/tokens.css already holds the house values. Replace the prototype literals in design-system.module.css (--lime, --accent-text, rgba(28,29,32,…), rgba(92,110,20,…), #2c2d31) with the token names. Move the sidebar to ink-deep.

Views to components.

  • Sidebar.tsx → .side .side-new .side-item .side-meter; the title bar gets .icon-btn pane toggles and the palette button
  • HomeView.tsx → .composer .ob-runsum .apv .listcard .banner; a first-run variant with the empty sidebar and inspector
  • SessionView.tsx, MessageBubble.tsx, DiffView.tsx → .vhead .msg .tool .diff .wait; the drawer has no component yet, and the backlog holds it
  • ApprovalCard.tsx → .apv with four states. The design-system entry gains a third ghost action (Allow for session) and a .kbd hint slot in each button
  • SandboxPopover.tsx, PermissionModePopover.tsx → one .ob-runsum summary + .pop with the three menus
  • CommandPalette.tsx → .pal .pal-row .pal__foot, the OpenWrite palette unchanged, with the terms index
  • WorkspacePane.tsx tabs → .tabs (Files · Changes · Terminal · Tool access); RightRail.tsx → .sk-rail .card .kv .meter with the wide state
  • ApplicationsView.tsx → .table as the main pane, with the inspector card .tabs Detail · Releases · Spend and .kv .chart .dialog .toast. Publish → .gates .form with Show log and the command line
  • AdministrationView.tsx → .form .switch-row .field--secret .table

Roles.

  • .btn and .gbtn are <button>.
  • .tabs is role="tablist". Each tab is role="tab" with aria-selected.
  • .tool__toggle is <button aria-expanded aria-controls>.
  • .menu-btn is <button aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded>.
  • .side-item is a link with aria-current="page".

Focus order on every screen: skip link → title bar → sidebar → view header → main → inspector → audit strip.

State. Color alone never shows a state. Each dot has a name. Each chip has a word.

Acceptance checks

  • Every screen keeps the audit strip, also in focus mode. Every id opens the log at that line.
  • An approval blocks the run until a person decides, and the decision appears in the audit within one second.
  • Allow-for-session, Pause, and Raise cap show a toast with Undo for 8 s, and Undo writes its own audit line.
  • Engine offline disables the composer and the banner clears on reconnect.
  • An approval left 30 min turns stale and pauses the session.
  • The state word is the same on the sidebar item, the view header, Home, and the audit line.
  • Every session, app, release, and audit id opens from ⌘K within two keystrokes.
  • Stop ends the turn within one second. The transcript stays.
  • A failed turn shows Retry turn and keeps the transcript.
  • Publish stays disabled until G5 passes. The disabled button is focusable and says which gates remain.
  • A failed gate stops the sequence and shows its finding with an evidence id.
  • Every gate row shows its elapsed time. The running gate counts up.
  • Changes can revert every changed file, with a toast and an audit line.
  • A failing app is visible in the Apps table and in the header counts.
  • A live app rolls back to the previous release in one action, runs no gates, and writes one audit line.
  • A re-run after a fix passes on the same draft.
  • Every control has a role and a name. Axe reports zero violations on the seven screens.
  • The cap stops the app: at 100% the app pauses and rejects every call. The composer turns disabled and shows the error banner.
  • Revoke needs the app name typed and stops the app at the next call.
  • The console renders from tokens only: no raw hex in a view file.
  • Under 900 px the sidebar folds into the drawer. The drawer traps focus, and Escape returns focus. Every action stays reachable by keyboard.
  • Mock engine is visible: the warn banner and the mock chip show, and nothing runs.

OpenWrite · the vault

Agents write rich documents. People read, correct, and approve.

OpenWrite is a local-first knowledge app for macOS. An agent writes Notes and Pages. A Note is a structured document with blocks, properties, links, and a shared theme. A Page is self-contained interactive markup in a sandbox. A person reads them in a calm three-pane workspace, organizes them, and approves anything the agent saves outside its folders. The agent pane opens when a run starts or an approval arrives.

Screens

Five screens, in the order a person meets them.

The first launch comes first. Then the workspace with a Note during a run, and the workspace with a Page and a decided approval. The command palette with the graph and Settings come last.

Flows

Five flows carry the product.

The agent writes a note

The main path.

  1. Ask. Type in the composer. The Scope button says where the note may go. Write note ⌘↩.idle
  2. Run. The agent pane opens if it was closed. An activity card appears with the streaming state and the elapsed time. The composer shows Stop run ⌘.streaming
  3. Land. The note appears in the list with the author dot. When the selection has not changed since Ask, the landed note becomes the selection. Otherwise the done card keeps Open note →.done
  4. Read. Open note selects it. The Reader shows the prose. The status bar shows words and backlinks.

A change outside the scope

The approval path.

  1. Ask. The agent wants Research/. The scope is Projects/.needs you
  2. See. The card says what the agent wants to create and why it waits. The agent chip reads needs you.
  3. Decide. Approve once, Deny, or Widen scope →. Deny shows an Undo toast for 8 s.
  4. Record. The card turns decided with your name and time. The activity keeps it for the day.decided

Today’s note

One shortcut. The app creates the note once.

  1. ⌘D. Today’s note opens. If it does not exist, the app creates it once. A toast at the bottom of the list pane reads "Today’s note created · Aug 28" for 4 s. The list then selects that row.created
  2. Exists. No toast. The list selects the row. The Reader scrolls to the top.exists
  3. Digest. The first time the note reads "Today is empty. Ask the agent for a digest." The agent’s morning digest links into it.

Read in focus

One note, nothing else.

  1. Open. Select a note. The Reader shows it.
  2. ⌘⇧F. Focus hides the Library, the list, and the agent pane in one action. The Reader centers the 760 measure. The toolbar keeps the crumb and Exit focus.focus
  3. Read. Nothing competes with the note. A new approval shows the 4 s toast "The agent needs you · Show →". Show leaves focus and opens the pane. Focus stays until you leave it.
  4. Esc. Esc or ⌘⇧F restores the previous pane set.restored

Narrow window

Four panes fold in a fixed order.

  1. Under 1340. The agent pane closes. The Agent button reads Agent · 1 while an approval waits.
  2. Under 1160. The Library collapses. The title-bar button brings it back as a drawer.
  3. Under 900. The list folds. A Show list button at the left of the Reader toolbar brings it back. The Reader keeps 420 px at least.

A toast "Denied #0413 · Undo" then shows 8 s at the bottom of the pane. Stale shows "Expired · run stopped · 07:30" with "Ask again →". Build notes

From the current app to this.

Where it lives

Tokens. Replace the values in DesignTokens.swift with the token block; keep the names; add live, gradient, and kindTag. Bundle Space Grotesk, IBM Plex Sans, and IBM Plex Mono (the Open Font License). Mirror the values in note-editor/theme.css as the --ow-* note contract.

First launch. On first launch, create the vault My notes under Application Support/OpenWrite/vaults/ and open it. Seed the two welcome notes. Do not ask. The first-run banner carries the provider step.

Panes to components.

  • LibraryPane.swift → .side .side-new .side-item .hash .side-meter
  • NoteListPane.swift → .input .row .row__meta .tag--kind .dot--agent
  • ReaderPane.swift → .crumb .menu-btn .gbtn .prose .statusbar; the theme dots become one .menu-btn with a .menu
  • PageRuntimeView.swift → the kind tag, Stop Page, Reload, and the status bar with capabilities
  • AgentPane.swift → .vhead--pane .act .apv .composer .toast, four approval states, closed at rest
  • CommandPaletteView.swift → .pal .pal-row with Recent, commands (Focus, Favorite, Move to folder, Add tag, Move to Trash), and notes in one list
  • LocalGraphView.swift → .dialog with the four-token plot; the legend reads tokens; backlinks when the wiki-link wire lands
  • OpenWriteSettingsView.swift → .form .select .switch-row .field--secret .callout

Key rule. One key does one thing in one place. ⌘↩ and ⌘⌫ act on the pane that has focus. In the composer they send. On a card they approve or deny. On a list row they move the note to the Trash. ⌘. stops the agent run. ⌘⇧. stops the Page.

Accessibility. Focus order: title bar → Library → list → Reader toolbar → Reader → Agent header → activity → composer. Every control follows the design-system role table and is 28 px tall or more. A dot without a word carries its name. The activity list is a polite live region. Reduced motion: the palette, the graph, and the drawer appear with a 120 ms fade and no slide. Cards do not lift.

Acceptance checks

  • Four panes at 1340 × 720. The collapse order is agent, Library, list.
  • Focus hides three panes in one action and Esc restores them.
  • At 1440 the prose column is 516 px wide with the agent pane open. It is 760 px wide with the pane closed.
  • The Library returns in one action from the title-bar button after any collapse.
  • Search reaches the body through FTS5 and keeps the Library filter.
  • An out-of-scope change waits. Approve once creates the note. The card then turns decided with a name and time.
  • Deny shows Undo for 8 s. Undo restores the waiting card.
  • ⌘⌫ moves a note to Trash when the list has focus. It denies a card when a card has focus. Undo restores the note.
  • A row dropped on Research/ moves the note and writes an activity line.
  • @agent filters the list to agent-authored rows and keeps the Library filter.
  • A Page runs with no network. Stop Page and Reload work. The status bar lists its capabilities.
  • The theme menu is labeled and Dark is ink with sky, not a third blue.
  • No provider shows the error callout and disables the composer. No run starts.
  • Activity survives a restart: the last 200 events return.
  • Every string uses Page, never Canvas.
  • No raw hex in a view: every color reads a token.
  • First launch opens a vault and shows the welcome note and the offline callout with no dialog.
  • Full Keyboard Access reaches every control and VoiceOver reads each state chip by its text.
  • A size change restyles the open note with no reload.
  • Export as a web page writes the rendered note to the vault exports folder.

OpenDictate · dictation for the whole Mac

Hold one key. Speak. Release. The words land where you type.

OpenDictate is on-device dictation for every app on a Mac. It lives in the menu bar. Setup takes three steps and ends with a spoken test. A small pill appears while you speak and tells you which app and which mode will receive the text. Cleanup runs on this Mac unless you choose a provider. Nothing leaves this Mac by default. v1 dictates. It does not transcribe recorded files.

PlatformNative macOS menu-bar app · Swift + Rust corewhisper.cpp on Metal or CoreML · optional cleanup through platform/gateway (Ollama or a provider)
WindowMain 960 × 800 · First run 720 × 560Pill 420 × 100 · menu-bar popover 320 wide
PeopleAnyone who types on a MacNo account for local use. Sign-in only for entitlements and, later, dictionary sync.
Ships inNo sibling checkout../opendictate is not beside this repository. core/ Rust · mac/ Swift · depends on platform/ only · not started

Map

A menu-bar icon, a popover, a pill, and one window.

The pill is the product. The popover is the fast path to it. The main window holds the setup and the dictation views, in the same pattern as the other apps. An ink-deep sidebar with two labeled groups sits beside a surface form. ⌘1 to ⌘7 open the views. Modes are configuration, not documents, so New mode belongs to the view header, not to the sidebar.

Rule · the pill never takes focus. Rule · the pill never covers the caret; it moves up by its own height if it would. Rule · esc cancels in every state. It keeps the text in History when the person keeps history on. Rule · one lower-case word in every state chip. Rule · the sidebar foot is the only privacy meter; a screen never repeats it.

Screens

Eight screens.

The screens come in the order a person meets them. First the three setup steps, then the three views people use most. The pill in context and every pill state with the popover come last.

Flows

Six flows carry the product.

Each step names the screen and the state the person sees. The numbers are the order; the chips are the state words the interface shows.

Setup

Three steps, offline, under five minutes.

  1. Permissions. Microphone and Accessibility, each with a live check. The step finishes when macOS grants it. A person can skip Accessibility.granted
  2. Model. Medium starts downloading at once. Continue turns enabled at once. Language and microphone are set here, with a live level.downloading
  3. Shortcut. ⌥ space by default; a conflict preselects the free key. Hold and say a few words. The words land in the Try it here field.tested
  4. Ready. The Ready panel says "Ready. Hold ⌥ space in any app." Done closes the window and opens the popover once. The menu-bar icon shows ready.

Dictate

The whole product in four seconds.

  1. Hold. The pill appears with the app and the mode it picked.listening
  2. Speak. Bars move; words appear. Silence shows "Listening…".
  3. Release. Transcribe, then clean up in the mode. Esc cancels. It keeps the text in History when the person keeps history on. ⌥ space inserts what you said, without cleanup.streaming
  4. Insert. The text lands at the caret. The pill says how many words, for 2 s.inserted
  5. Undo or review. ⌘Z in the app, or Undo in the popover, removes exactly the insert. Review opens the popover with the text.

Hands-free

For a paragraph or a page.

  1. Press twice. A second press within 300 ms of a release locks hands-free, whatever the length of the first press. The pill shows the hands-free chip and a running timer.hands-free
  2. Speak. After 20 words the pill grows to two lines. Say "new paragraph" or pause 3 s.
  3. Press. One press stops and inserts. Esc cancels. It keeps the text in History when the person keeps history on.inserted

Fix a word

The app learns from what you correct.

  1. Notice. "Turbopuffer" came out wrong. You retype it right after the insert.
  2. Offer. After the first correction, the popover shows one ghost line: "Add ‘Turbopuffer’ to the dictionary."offer
  3. Suggest. After three corrections, Dictionary shows the word in the learned-words callout.suggestion
  4. Add. One click. The next dictation uses it.added

Change how text reads

Modes and app rules, without a prompt to write.

  1. Pick. Modes › Email. Set Full cleanup and Plain and direct. Each change saves at once.
  2. Preview. The callout shows what you said and what Email writes.
  3. Rule. Mail → Email. The pill shows Email whenever Mail is in front.saved

Cleanup leaves the Mac

Only when you choose it, and always visible.

  1. Choose. Modes › Runs on › a provider with your key. A warn callout says text is sent.provider
  2. See. The chip row on the pill names the provider, on every dictation. The sidebar foot counts words sent.
  3. Fail safe. Provider offline: the pill says "Inserted 9 words in Mail, with no cleanup. Anthropic did not answer." The sidebar foot shows "provider offline" until the next success.provider offline

Build notes

From nothing to this.

Where it lives

Shape. core/ in Rust: audio capture → whisper.cpp (Metal or CoreML) → optional cleanup through platform/gateway (Ollama or a provider). mac/ in Swift holds NSStatusItem for the icon and popover. An NSPanel at status level never activates. The overlay layer draws the pill. SwiftUI windows cover first run and the main app. AXUIElement inserts, with a clipboard fallback. UniFFI binds core to the app. No daemon, no socket.

Tokens. A Tokens.swift generated from the design-system token block. Bundle the three faces (the Open Font License). The pill and the popover read the ink ground. The main window reads the surface ground with an ink-deep sidebar.

Views to components.

  • First run → .sk-steps .listcard .chip .radio .meter .select .input .callout
  • Main window → .side .side-item .vhead .form .switch-row .select .table .listcard .tag .callout .empty
  • Pill → .od-pill .od-mic .od-wave .od-text .chip .kbd .btn--ghost
  • Popover → .pop--bar .chip .switch .listcard .gbtn .dot--wait

Acceptance checks

  • The pill appears within 80 ms of key-down and never takes focus from the app.
  • Setup completes with no account. Dictation runs offline after the model download. Setup ends with a spoken test that inserts into the setup window.
  • Setup never waits on a download. Continue is enabled on every step while Medium downloads.
  • Insert works in TextEdit, Mail, Notes, Slack, VS Code, Xcode, Terminal, and a browser text field. The clipboard fallback says so in the pill.
  • Esc cancels at every state. Canceled text appears in History when the person keeps history on.
  • ⌘Z removes exactly the inserted text, nothing more.
  • The app rule picks the mode. The pill shows it before the first word.
  • A dictionary word is recognized in the next dictation without a restart.
  • Zero words leave the Mac with cleanup on this Mac or off, and the sidebar foot proves it.
  • Provider offline inserts the words with no cleanup and says so.
  • VoiceOver announces the strings in the Announcements row. Reduce Motion stops the pulse and the bars.

Borrowed, then fixed

Superwhisper and Wispr Flow prove the model. Hold a key, speak, and get text in any app, with modes and a dictionary. Their setup and their floating windows are where people get lost. This schematic keeps the model and fixes the two weak spots.

IdeaSuperwhisperWispr FlowOpenDictate
Hold to talkHold a shortcut, release to insertHold fn; tap fn twice for hands-freeOne shortcut, ⌥ space by default. Hold to talk. Press twice for hands-free. The pill always shows which of the two is active and how to stop.
ModesCustom model modes with promptsAuto-edits and writing stylesModes with app rules. Each mode is three plain switches and a cleanup level, with a before-and-after preview. Mail gets Email, Xcode gets Code, without asking.
Dictionary and snippetsCustom vocabularyPersonal dictionary, snippetsA dictionary of word · say it like · kind, snippets with a trigger phrase, and learned words. The app notices what you correct and offers to add it.
The floating windowA floating window, centered when off screenThe Flow Bar at the bottomThe pill: bottom center, never over the caret, never takes focus. It shows the target app, the mode, the audio, the running text, the timer, and the two keys that matter. Esc cancels in every state. ⌘Z undoes after insert.
SetupPermissions, models, shortcut across settingsOnboarding in the HubThree steps in one window. Steps pair permissions with live checks, a model with a download meter, and a shortcut with a spoken test. Setup never waits on the download. Ready in under five minutes, offline.
Words while you speakApple Dictation types live at the caret, so the document changes as you talkThe Flow Bar holds the words until you stopThe running text stays in the pill. Nothing enters the document until you release, and esc leaves the document exactly as it was.
A recorded fileMacWhisper: drop a file, get a transcript with speaker labels and SRTDictation onlyNot in v1. OpenDictate dictates. Transcribing a recorded file is a different job, and v1 says so rather than doing it badly.
HistoryRecordings listHistory in the HubHistory with search terms, copy, and insert again. The last dictation is one click away in the menu-bar popover.
